title: This Robot Can Flap Its Wings and Swim
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyThis Robot Can Flap Its Wings and SwimBeing able to both fly and swim isn’t easy—but the FAAV does itDNBy David Nield3:00 PM CDT on July 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleImagine being a researcher wanting to take a closer look at the 80 percent of the ocean that remains unexplored: You drive to the coast, unpack a winged robot from your trunk, and then throw it into the air to take flight. Then comes the clever part: Once your robot reaches the area of the ocean you want to measure, it dives beneath the waves.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 00:00/01:0610205.7K 350The World Is Facing a Huge Plastic Crisis in the OceansShareNextStayThat scenario isn’t possible now, but we’re a big step closer to it thanks to a new “flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle” (FAAV) developed by engineers at MIT and Swiss Federal Technology Institute of Lausanne, in Switzerland. They’ve published a study of their work in Science.The FAAV takes inspiration from the more than 100 species of bird that can also swim through water (for instance, loons, gulls, puffins, and petrels). The robot is both lightweight (less than half a pound) and fully hydrophobic, characteristics that make it able to transition from one state to another and back again.Already have an account?Log inJoin to continue readingYou've run out of free articles.
